_readme: Copy this file to the ROOT of a brand kit folder (beside its Portrait/ and
Landscape/ folders) and rename it to brand.json.
It carries everything about a brand that is words rather than artwork, so a kit
is genuinely swappable: point the app at a different folder and the covers,
filenames, PDF metadata and page stamps all follow.
Anything left empty is simply not printed. The disclaimer and tagline are blank
here on purpose: the task briefs ask for a 'tagline' and a 'standard disclaimer'
without giving the words, which live in the rebranding SOP. Paste the approved
wording in rather than approximating it.
Each page stamp also has its own checkbox in the app. Wording here plus the
matching toggle switched on is what puts a stamp on the page.
FIELDS
name / slug        brand name on covers and in PDF metadata; slug in filenames
tagline            e.g. the line the Budget Mailboxes brief asks for
disclaimer         the SOP's standard disclaimer, stamped on every page
version_label      defaults to 'Version 1.0'
last_updated       leave empty to use the run's own month, e.g. 'Last Updated
August 2026'; set it to pin a fixed value
attribution        {manufacturer} and {brand} are substituted
manufacturer_aliases   fixes for values the review sheet gets wrong. A
manufacturer that is a website, the seller, or the brand
itself is dropped rather than printed, so an alias is how
you rescue one — e.g. {"Florencemailboxes.com": "Florence
Corporation"}
stamp_ink / stamp_bg   '#rrggbb' overrides. Leave empty and the stamp colour
is read from the kit's own artwork.
name: Budget Mailboxes
